content:
Heads up: this picture is 76 days old — the last transaction captured was 2026-03-28, so treat everything below as where things stood then, not today.

On the goal: £15,000 safety net by 2027-06-01, with £3,000 already banked. That leaves £12,000 to go across roughly 14 months. At free cash flow of £1,774 a month, the raw capacity is there — the goal needs around £857 a month to hit the date, and your cash flow clears that comfortably. You're not behind; you're in a position to run ahead of pace if the spending holds.

The data here is thin — only 6 transactions across 87 days, so no behavioural patterns have formed yet. What the numbers do show is that **housing** is the dominant outflow at £2,700 across the window, which is expected and fixed. **Eating & drinking out** ran at £73 a month as of late March — small in the scheme of things, but it's the one discretionary category with room to move.

A trim of £18 a month on eating & drinking out won't shift the finish line on its own, but it locks in a habit of directing surplus toward the goal rather than away from it.

[CTA:cut_lever]Trim 18 from eating & drinking out[/CTA]

— C.
